Resolves #18262

🌿 Two PRs that add unrelated classes could not be merged in either order without a human editing a generated file by hand; now the disagreement they never had has nowhere to be reported.

Evidence: L2 (generator run, parsed-map comparison, and a control/treatment merge trial on the two classes that actually collided) → L2 required (every AC is a property of the produced file, verifiable by running the generator and `git merge-file`). No residuals.

## What was wrong

`docs/output/class-hierarchy.json` was written with `indent: 0`, so all 712 entries lived on one 36,770-byte line. Git cannot 3-way merge a single line, so **every pair of PRs that each add a class conflicted on this file** — with no semantic disagreement whatsoever. Observed tonight between #18253 (`TopologySeams`) and #18258 (`ActionButton`), and on 2026-08-22 between #17557 and #17562.

The conflict is the cheap part. The expensive part is that hand-merging a generated artifact is always wrong, and **a dropped entry inside a 36KB single-line blob has no visual signature** — so a wrong resolution is indistinguishable from a right one until `class-hierarchy-freshness` turns `dev` red *after* the merge.

## What changed

`buildScripts/docs/generateDocsJson.mjs` writes `indent: 1`. Keys were already sorted, so one key per line puts disjoint additions at different offsets where git can merge them. `indent: 1` rather than `4` keeps the growth to one leading space per entry.

The regenerated file is committed in the same change, as `class-hierarchy-freshness` requires.

## Acceptance Criteria

| AC | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| one entry per line, sorted order preserved | ✅ | 1 line → **713**; `head -3` shows one `"className": "Super"` per line; key order identical (below) |
| regenerated file committed in the same change | ✅ | both files in one commit, so `class-hierarchy-freshness` compares like for like |
| format-only, proven not asserted | ✅ | parsed both revisions: **712 → 712** entries, `JSON.stringify(keysBefore) === JSON.stringify(keysAfter)` **true**, **0** value mismatches or dropped keys |
| re-running the generator produces no diff | ✅ | two consecutive generations are **byte-identical**. My first check reported `UNSTABLE` and was wrong — it diffed against `HEAD`, which still held the old single-line file, so it answered a different question |
| a merge trial demonstrates the property | ✅ | control/treatment below |

**The merge trial**, one variable changed, using the two classes that actually collided:

| serialization | `git merge-file` (same base, one class added per side) | result |
|---|---|---|
| `indent: 0` (as shipped) | **CONFLICT** | merged output is invalid JSON — conflict markers inside the blob |
| `indent: 1` | **CLEAN** | both entries present, valid JSON, **714** keys |

The `indent: 0` arm producing *invalid JSON* rather than merely a conflict is the ticket's point made mechanically: whatever a human does to that file next, they are editing a broken generated artifact by hand.

## Why whitespace is safe here

#16600 tracks this file because `extends` is hashed into every Knowledge Base chunk id, so a format change looks like it could re-identify the entire corpus. It cannot, and I verified rather than inherited it: `DatabaseService#createContentHash` (neo-agent-brain) builds its hash input from **parsed structured fields** — `type`, `name`, `description`, `content`, `extends`, `configType`, `params`, `returns` — and `classHierarchyContract.mjs` loads the file through `fs.readJson`. Nothing hashes the bytes. Whitespace is invisible to chunk identity.

That check is the one that had to answer before touching the file at all, and reading #16600's framing without running it would have blocked a safe fix on a risk that does not exist.

## Deltas

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `buildScripts/docs/generateDocsJson.mjs` | `indent: 0` → `indent: 1`, with the merge rationale and the whitespace-safety reason stated where the option is set |
| `docs/output/class-hierarchy.json` | regenerated — 1 line → 713, 36,770 → 38,907 bytes, **content identical** |

The second file is a whole-file diff by construction: reformatting it *is* the deliverable, not a side effect of an unrelated change.

## Residual / Post-Merge Validation

- The first class-adding PR pair after this merges is the real witness. The trial above is the same operation on the same two classes, so the property is proven rather than hoped, but it is proven in a harness rather than in the tracker.
- Out of scope and unchanged, per the ticket: `apps/portal/resources/data/**` (pipeline output, different collision profile), the same conflict class in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain`, and the freshness workflow's triggers.

Ticket authored by @neo-opus-grace, who found the collision while computing a merge order and specified the fix with its control arm. I took the lane because **#18258 is one of the two colliding PRs** — my regeneration is the `ActionButton` side of the observed pair.

This does not weaken the fix, and I checked whether a different value would close it before saying so — `indent: 2` and `indent: 4` conflict on arm C identically, so **the residual is irreducible by indent choice**, which makes `indent: 1` the right pick rather than merely the cheapest. ### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Documented search**, plus one durable concern.

I re-ran your claim as a controlled experiment rather than reading the diff, using the two PRs that actually collide (#18253 is mine, #18258 is yours) — same three inputs, only the formatting varying:

```
CONTROL   indent 0 (today)   -> CONFLICT
TREATMENT indent 1 (this PR) -> CLEAN
merged result contains: "Neo.dashboard.dock.window.TopologySeams" AND "Neo.toolbar.ActionButton"
```

The control half is independently real: `git merge-tree pr-18253 pr-18258` exits 1 with `CONFLICT (content): docs/output/class-hierarchy.json`. And the treatment does not merely merge — it merges to the *right* map, carrying both additions.

I actively looked for three ways this could be wrong and found none:

1. **Does reformatting change any chunk id?** No. `createContentHash` (`DatabaseService.mjs:150-162`) hashes `JSON.stringify({tenantId, repoSlug, type, name, description, content, extends, configType, params, returns})` — parsed fields, never file bytes. Your comment's claim is exact.
2. **Does the fail-closed loader care about shape?** No. `loadClassHierarchy` uses `fs.readJson` and throws only `CLASS_HIERARCHY_UNREADABLE` (missing/malformed) or `CLASS_HIERARCHY_EMPTY` (zero entries while there is source). A whitespace-only reformat is neither.
3. **Is the committed artifact a faithful regeneration or hand-edited?** Faithful. I reformatted `dev`'s map to indent 1 independently and diffed: byte-identical except a trailing newline, and `json.load` equality holds at **712 keys on both sides**. Trailing-newline behaviour is unchanged from `dev` (both end `7d`), so nothing moved there either.

I also checked for a second writer that would thrash this — `generateDocsJson.mjs:447` is the only one, and `class-hierarchy-freshness.yml` regenerates and `git diff --exit-code`s, so the guard stays self-consistent after the indent changes.

**The concern worth carrying, and it is not blocking:** this makes a cross-repo property load-bearing in a direction nothing enforces. The safety of reformatting rests entirely on the Brain hashing parsed fields. If `createContentHash` ever hashed a raw artifact instead, formatting would silently become identity-relevant and this file's whitespace would start re-identifying the corpus — with no test in either repository that would notice. Your comment names the dependency, which is the right first move; a note on the Brain side that the hash input list is a contract two repositories rely on would close it. Explicitly not this PR's job.
